scenario.name: Local inert certutil decode variants
scenario.description: Four new scope-checked runs cover five of six grounded local-decode use cases: ordinary base64 decode, hexadecimal decode, forced DLL-named output with -f, standard-user context, and slash-form syntax. Decode followed by execution remains future work. The unprovable historical run is not current evidence.

coverage.grounding: Independent audit at c23e800 plus the four routed, newly executed scenarios
coverage.assessment: The four new runs close every explicitly routed execution requirement and bring grounded coverage above the 60% gate floor. Decode-then-execute remains a separately scoped future scenario because it changes the safety profile.

environment.isolation: Each valid scenario began from a separate rollback to win_verify_baseline. All commands were local file-to-file transforms with no network destination.

sensors.name: Sysmon
sensors.config_notes: Verification-grade unfiltered process, network, DNS, file, and registry coverage; LSASS ProcessAccess EID 10 enabled.

tool.name: certutil.exe
tool.source: Built into the target operating system

observed_techniques.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
observed_techniques.observation: Certutil decoded inert base64 and hexadecimal fixtures with dash and slash syntax, under SYSTEM and a standard user, and every output hash matched the expected marker bytes.

registry.assessment: Three CryptDllFindOIDInfo OID leaf keys and their Name values were initialized; this is legitimate context-sensitive API state, not a decode rule.

process_identity.assessment: Sysmon captured certutil identity, -decodehex, paths, hashes, SYSTEM user, and System integrity.

parent_child.assessment: No decoded output execution or direct child was observed.

rule_results.sigma/win_file_event_certutil_suspicious: did not fire: .bin is outside the executable/script tier

scenario.name: Forced base64 decode to a DLL-named inert output
scenario.design_section: Verified flow 2: forced decode to a payload extension

registry.assessment: Same three SYSTEM-context OID leaf keys and Name values.

process_identity.assessment: Sysmon captured -f -decode and the DLL-named output path.

parent_child.assessment: The inert DLL-named output was neither loaded nor executed.

rule_results.sigma/win_file_event_certutil_suspicious: fired: first lab positive for the executable/script tier

scenario.name: Base64 decode under a local standard user

environment.account_context: Temporary local Users-group member; not in Administrators; Medium integrity. Log on as a batch job was granted for this run and removed by snapshot rollback.
environment.collection_note: The wrapper's initial combined export stopped partway. The unchanged event channels were re-exported for the exact five-second run window; the committed evidence records the recovered export hashes.

command.completion_assessment: Task Scheduler LastTaskResult was 0 and the output hash matched the expected inert bytes.

registry.assessment: The three SYSTEM OID leaf creations and three Name writes were absent. The user process produced nine OID ancestor EID 12 events and per-user MuiCache initialization instead.

process_identity.assessment: Sysmon captured WIN10-ANALYSIS\certlab at Medium integrity with the complete -decode command.

parent_child.assessment: Certutil launched only its console host; decoded output was not executed.

context_diff_against_system.output_path: SYSTEM outputs were under C:\lab; the user output was under C:\Users\certlab.
context_diff_against_system.registry: SYSTEM produced 3 OID leaf CreateKey plus 3 Name SetValue events; the standard user produced zero of those six leaf events.

rule_results.sigma/win_file_event_certutil_suspicious: did not fire: .txt is outside the executable/script tier

registry.assessment: Same three SYSTEM-context OID leaf keys and Name values.

process_identity.assessment: This Windows build accepted /decode. The old plain-contains selector missed it; the windash selector matches it.

parent_child.assessment: No decoded output execution or direct child was observed.

rule_results.sigma/win_process_creation_certutil_deco: fired after windash fix; predecessor rule did not fire
rule_results.sigma/win_file_event_certutil_suspicious: did not fire: .bin is outside the executable/script tier

precision_measurement.provenance: audit iteration 3 precision/precision-input.json plus the auditor's any-certutil-start control
precision_measurement.interpretation: The control also had zero clean hits, so the result is null rather than evidence that certutil decode is absent in production.

precision_measurement.provenance: audit iteration 3 exact harness measurement of the corrected eight-extension rule
precision_measurement.interpretation: The corrected rule has zero clean hits and one attack-corpus EID 11 hit for AllTheThings.dll. Deployment tooling can still reconstruct benign binaries, so the reconciled posture is medium FP likelihood, hunt, level medium.

precision_measurement.provenance: audit iteration 3 exact harness measurement of the corrected four-extension rule, plus the any-certutil-file-write control
precision_measurement.interpretation: The zero is a null result. Legitimate certutil TXT, DAT, BIN, and ZIP output makes high FP likelihood the production judgement.

safety_validation.scenario_scope: safety/check-scenario-scope.py returned PASS with no findings after the scenario edits.
safety_validation.third_party_code: none; only the OS-builtin Microsoft-signed certutil and lab-authored inert fixture/runner scripts were used

audit_gate.scenario_coverage: 5/6 grounded local-decode use cases (83%, above the 0.6 floor)
non_blocking_findings: Decode followed by execution or loading remains a separately scoped future scenario.
The ambient data/text file-event rule has no positive corpus sample; its recall is supported by lab evidence, not the EVTX corpus.

validation.json: verification.json and all committed evidence JSON files passed JSON validation on 2026-08-10.

sanitization.notes: Only selected telemetry fields, hashes, timestamps, aggregate counts, lab topology, and inert fixture content are committed. Raw exports remain outside the repository.

historical_context.note: The original SYSTEM base64-to-TXT run had no retained raw export and cannot be given retrospective scope proof. The new standard-user base64 run independently covers ordinary -decode with a retained, scope-checked export.
